<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="UTF-8">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
<!-- Content-Security-Policy backstop. This file is SHIPPED (opened over file:// or a
     local static server), and it renders universe content that our own generators
     wrote, so the policy is delivered as a meta tag rather than a response header.

     NOTE FOR EDITORS: do not write a literal script start-tag anywhere in this comment
     or in any other markup above the real one. Both the audit render check
     (sot.check_viewer_renders) and the runtime harness (evals/audit/viewer_runtime.js)
     locate the embedded program by scanning for the first script start-tag in the file,
     so a mention of one inside a comment feeds them a slice of HTML and every universe
     starts reporting "Viewer does not render". Say "script element" in prose.

     default-src 'none' blocks every fetch and navigation class not named below: no
     connect/fetch/XHR/beacon, no remote programs, no remote stylesheets, no remote
     images, no remote fonts, no workers. A universe viewer must never reach the live
     public internet, both because the data is synthetic-but-personal and because a
     tag that survives build-time neutralisation must still be inert here.

     Named exceptions, each load-bearing:
       script-src 'unsafe-inline'  the viewer IS one inline script element, and 28
                                   controls use inline onclick= handlers. A nonce covers
                                   the block but NOT the attribute handlers, so a nonce
                                   would render the UI dead. A script element planted in
                                   universe content is still inert: it arrives through
                                   innerHTML, which never executes one, and the single
                                   raw markup sink (the SVG file preview) is stripped at
                                   build time by build_viewer.neutralize_markup.
       style-src 'unsafe-inline'   the base stylesheet below plus inline style= attrs.
       img-src / media-src / frame-src 'self' data: blob: file:
                                   filesystem previews are data: URIs and relative
                                   paths under seed_data_files_rendered/. file: is
                                   named explicitly because 'self' does not match
                                   sibling file:// URLs in Chrome.
       font-src data:              no remote webfont may be fetched.
       form-action 'none' / base-uri 'none'
                                   nothing can be submitted anywhere, and no injected
                                   base element can re-point the relative preview URIs.

     The two Google Fonts preconnect hints and the Google Fonts stylesheet that used to
     sit here were removed with this policy. They were the viewer's only live-internet
     contact, the stylesheet is blocked by style-src anyway, and a preconnect hint is
     NOT governed by CSP in Chrome, so leaving them would have kept the exact leak this
     policy exists to close. Typography falls back to the local stacks already declared
     in --font-display / --font-body / --font-mono below. -->
<meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" content="default-src 'none'; script-src 'unsafe-inline'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data: blob: file:; media-src 'self' data: blob: file:; font-src data:; frame-src 'self' data: blob: file:; form-action 'none'; base-uri 'none'">
